title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator on mobile takes notes of in-person conversations with speaker attribution
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned mobile speaker attribution feature from existing Facilitator and Teams Rooms capabilities. The roadmap facts, licensing statements and availability path are supported; targeted searches did not find the mobile-specific defaults, controls or storage details it identifies as unpublished.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not confirm that the documented availability setting governs phone-started note-taking or speaker attribution.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "mobile" "default" "control"; Facilitator mobile in-person notes storage access retention Loop transcription policy. Read manage-apps and facilitator-teams; neither explicitly places phone-started capture under the availability setting.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page gives Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page says Facilitator is allowed by default unless all apps are blocked.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default. However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: Learn lists mobile capture of ad-hoc discussions and action items as generally available.
claims.quote: The following Facilitator capabilities are currently generally available: ... Mobile capture of ad-hoc discussions and action items

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the mobile speaker attribution change itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "mobile" "speaker"; Facilitator Teams mobile speaker attribution storage default licensing admin control. Read facilitator-teams and facilitator-teams-rooms; the former lists mobile capture, while speaker attribution detail concerns Rooms.

claims.claim: Loop experiences in Teams control AI-generated meeting notes through the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled PowerShell setting.
claims.quote: Loop experiences in Teams control AI-generated notes for meetings, which are enabled by default. You can manage this control using the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled setting in PowerShell.

claims.claim: The IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled setting applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: This setting applies to your entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.
